name: The Ghost of Christmas Past
description: The first of Scrooge's three spirits: a flickering figure, child and old man at once, with a light streaming from its head
origin: A Christmas Carol by Charles Dickens
legend: When the clock strikes one, the curtains of Scrooge's bed are drawn aside by the first spirit. It looks like a child, and yet like an old man seen from a great way off. It wears a white tunic trimmed with summer flowers, holds a branch of fresh green holly, and from the crown of its head springs a bright clear jet of light. Under its arm it carries a great extinguisher for a cap. It leads Scrooge back through his own past: the schoolroom where he was left alone at Christmas, his sister Fan coming to fetch him home, the ball at old Fezziwig's warehouse, and the day Belle released him from their engagement because he loved money more. Scrooge can bear no more, seizes the extinguisher-cap and presses it down over the spirit's head, but he can't hide the light.

myths.claim: The Ghost of Christmas Past is a child.
myths.explanation: Dickens says it is like a child, yet not so like a child as like an old man. Its hair is white with age, and its face has not a wrinkle.

myths.claim: It shows Scrooge other people's Christmases long ago.
myths.explanation: Scrooge asks whether it means the long past, and it answers: his own.
He presses the extinguisher-cap down with all his force, but the light still streams out from under it across the floor.

myths.claim: A light shines from the top of its head.
myths.explanation: A bright clear jet of light springs from the crown of its head, which is why it carries an extinguisher for a cap.

quotes.text: These are but shadows of the things that have been. They have no consciousness of us.
quotes.speaker: The Ghost of Christmas Past

powers: Walking through years as if through doors
A light that can't be put out
Showing a man what he once was
Flight, with a touch of its hand
weaknesses: A great extinguisher for a cap
Only an hour to work in
A pupil who can't bear to look
legacy: Played as a child, an old man, a woman and a candle flame in adaptations, since the book allows all of them
The pattern for every story in which a character is walked back through their own memories
facts: The Ghost of Christmas Past is the first of the three spirits to visit Scrooge
It arrives as the clock strikes one
It looks like a child and like an old man at the same time
It holds a branch of fresh green holly, and its dress is trimmed with summer flowers
A bright clear jet of light springs from the crown of its head
It carries a great extinguisher for a cap under its arm
Its shape flickers: now one arm, now one leg, now twenty legs
It shows Scrooge his lonely schooldays, his sister Fan, Fezziwig's ball and his lost love Belle
hostIntro: Our next guest has brought the holiday slides. All of them. Yours, I'm afraid. Do sit down.
